title: retrieval-citation-sanity-prompt-suite
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a focused prompt/test-suite and regression checks aimed at measuring citation fidelity for retrieval-augmented responses. Goal is to produce a compact, reproducible set of queries and scoring rules we can run automatically during model onboarding and weekly regression runs.

Scope and motivation:
- Focus: "retrieval + answer + explicit citation" workflows used by product teams that require high provenance (help centers, legal faqs, docs search).
- Key behaviors to validate: grounding (is the answer supported by a retrieved doc), quote accuracy (verbatim or near-verbatim quoting when asked), and refusal/abstain behavior when no reliable source exists.
- This is intentionally narrower than full semantic correctness; emphasis is provenance correctness and no-misattribution.

High-level acceptance criteria (onboarding target):
- Citation precision >= 0.80 (token-level overlap of returned quote with source span)
- Quote verbatim match >= 0.75 for explicit-quote prompts
- Hallucination rate <= 0.05 (cases where model asserts a source that has no supporting text)
- Refusal F1 >= 0.85 on no-source / contradictory-source prompts
If a candidate model falls short on any metric, it goes into a remediation loop: prompt/template tuning -> re-eval -> if still fail, model variant blocked from production routing.

Eval harness and data flow (implementation notes):
- Input: (prompt, retrieval set) pairs. The retrieval set is a deterministic list of 10-30 doc snippets sampled from a simulated index (see dataset section). The harness inserts the top-k snippets into the prompt following the product template.
- Execution: call candidate model via internal eval endpoint with streaming disabled (we need stable full-text outputs), capture model text and structured-citation fields if available.
- Postprocess: align returned citations to the doc corpus using exact URL match and fuzzy span-matching for quoted substrings. Compute metrics below.
- Repeat for 1k prompts per run (mix of in-distribution + adversarial). Runs should be fast (< 2h for ci-weekly).

Prompt templates (examples):
1) Short answer + quote + cite:
"Using only the provided documents, answer this question and include a quoted excerpt that supports your answer, then list the source in the format [title] - [url]. If you cannot find a reliable source, reply 'NO RELIABLE SOURCE FOUND' and do not guesses."
2) Explain and attribute:
"Summarize how X works according to the documents below. For each assertion, attach a bracketed citation (title - url). Only use the documents; do not invent facts."
3) Explicit refusal test:
"Does the provided corpus contain an official limit for Y? If yes provide the exact sentence and citation; if not, return exactly: NO RELIABLE SOURCE FOUND"
4) Partial quote preference test:
"Find any sentence that mentions 'Z feature' and return the exact sentence and its source. If multiple sentences match, prefer the one from the highest-confidence doc (see doc.metadata.confidence)."

Representative testcases (toy examples included inline for clarity):
- TC1 (grounded, single-source): prompt about 'How long is the trial period for Pro Account?' retrieval contains an FAQ snippet: 'Pro Account trial period is 30 days.' Expected: answer = '30 days' with quote exact and citation pointing to faq/pro-account.html.
- TC2 (near-duplicate sources): two docs both paraphrase the same line; model should cite the doc that contains the verbatim phrase if prompt asks for exact quote; otherwise either cite either but not fabricate.
- TC3 (no source): question about deprecated policy not present in retrieval. Expected: 'NO RELIABLE SOURCE FOUND' only.
- TC4 (contradictory snippets): two retrieved snippets say different numbers. Model should either: (a) avoid answering and ask clarifying question, or (b) report the conflict with both citations. At minimum, should not invent a third number.
- TC5 (misattribution trap): retrieval includes doc A containing a passage paraphrasing doc B but doc A metadata claims B as a reference. If model returns the passage and attributes to B while the exact text live in A, penalize as false attribution.

Scoring definitions (deterministic):
- Citation Precision: Given the returned quoted substring, compute token-level overlap with the matched source span. (overlap_tokens / returned_tokens).
- Quote Verbatim Match: exact-match fraction (character normalized) for cases tagged as 'explicit-quote' prompts. Allow whitespace and punctuation normalization.
- Grounding Recall: fraction of assertions in answer that are supported by at least one retrieved doc span (binary per assertion).
- Attribution Accuracy: URL/title pair must match the doc where the supporting text originates. Exact match required.
- Refusal Correctness: precision/recall of returning 'NO RELIABLE SOURCE FOUND' in no-source cases.
- False-Attribution Rate: percent of cases where the model attaches a citation but matching span in cited doc is missing.

Thresholds and severity rules:
- Critical fail: False-Attribution Rate > 0.02 OR Hallucination rate > 0.10 => block model from onboarding.
- High priority: Citation Precision < 0.7 OR Refusal F1 < 0.7 => block until fix.
- Warnings: small drops (5-10%) relative to baseline trigger deeper analysis but not immediate block.

Dataset / corpus construction (for eval):
- Core corpus: 3k curated help center/articles extracted from product docs with canonical urls. Include doc metadata: title, url, published_date, authority_score (0-1).
- Adversarial set: 600 crafted snippets with partial matches, paraphrases, and misleading attributions. These are synthetic but hand-reviewed.
- Held-out weekly test: 1k prompts sampled from product support logs (anonymized) + 200 adversarial.
- For each doc snippet we also store the canonical source span offsets to enable precise overlap scoring.

Regression monitoring and alerting:
- Baseline: onboarding baseline stored per-model-arch (e.g., llama-3-13b-8k/q4f32) with nightly runs. Save metric history in metrics-store (time series).
- Alert rules: if Citation Precision or Quote Verbatim Match drops more than 5 percentage points over 7-day rolling average OR if False-Attribution Rate increases by absolute 0.5 percentage points, create an incident in ENG-APPLIED-ML and notify #applied-ml-alerts.
- Debug artifacts produced per-failed-case: full prompt, retrieval payload, model response, matched doc spans, scoring trace. Attach to incident.

Integration checklist (how to wire into CI/CD):
- [ ] Add suite to onboarding pipeline next to safety/regression tests.
- [ ] Ensure eval job uses stable retrieval seeds (deterministic) and deterministic top-k selection.
- [ ] Register baseline metrics for new model family and store in model-registry metadata.
- [ ] Add postprocessing job to compute token-level overlaps using tokenization canonicalization (we use BPE-v2 canonicalizer).

Known limitations / caveats:
- Token-level overlap is sensitive to tokenization differences across model families; enforce canonicalization step.
- Some product templates expect paraphrase summaries (not verbatim quotes); those prompts must be excluded from quote-precision metrics and have separate thresholds.
- Retrieval quality dominates many failures; separate out retrieval failures vs. model hallucination in the reporting UI.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Should we require explicit span offsets in the model output (e.g., source:start:end) to simplify scoring? Pros: deterministic scoring. Cons: product teams worried about verbosity. Team to decide by 2025-03-01.
- TODO: build 200 synthetic adversarial cases that specifically try to elicit confident but wrong URL attributions (owner: Marco).
- TODO: run a 1k-sample A/B between candidate model + template variants to pick best template for citation prompts (owner: Leah).

Quick examples (sample prompt -> expected model output):
1) Prompt: "What is the max file size for uploads? Use the documents and include a quoted line and source."
Expected: "Max upload size is 250 MB"
Quote: "\"Maximum file upload: 250 MB per file.\""
Source: "Help Center - Uploads - https://docs.redwood.ai/help/uploads#max-size"
2) Prompt (no-source): "Is there a policy that allows us to override retention for user A?"
Expected: "NO RELIABLE SOURCE FOUND"

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc focused and link to the larger onboarding PRD rather than copy-paste.
- After we stabilize metrics, propose adding a "provenance confidence" field to the API so downstream apps can gate UI behavior.

End of doc. (Working draft — expect iterations; please add examples in comments or Slack @aisha).
